The prior G187/kinematics notes were the 2026-05-31 state.

jobsSchemaNote: Operations match the master_post_hurco_v11 zod schema (camActionSchemas.ts L113-139): operation_type, tool_number, tool_diameter_mm, tool_flutes, material_iso (P/M/K/N/S/H), spindle_rpm, feed_mm_min, axial_depth_mm, coordinates[{x,y,z,type}]. material_iso=P (steel, kc1.1=1800) — JM Die's most common group. Dims are mm (engine is mm-native); config.units=metric keeps each job internally consistent. These mill jobs serve the mill posts (hurco standalone/agi, haas-vf2, okuma-genos-osp); lathe/mill-turn posts (lb3000/multus/winmax-lathe) need their own turning-op job set (od_rough/tool_orientation/insert_radius_mm) — added in the fleet-coverage phase.

jobs.label: Canned drilling cycle (op.cycle -> G81 modal; exercises the canned-cycle path on Fanuc-family posts)
Rigid-tap canned cycle (op.cycle.type:tap -> G84 modal; all 4 mill posts emit bare G84, NO M29)
jobs.notes: operation_type is 'drill' (not 'tap') so the canned-cycle gate fires in Hurco/Okuma engines (gate: drill||bore). cycle.type:'tap' routes to G84 inside emitCannedCycle for all 4 engines. feed_mm_min=375 = pitch(0.75mm) x rpm(500) -- rigid-tap feed contract. Haas: bare G84, always rigid, NO M29 (M29 on Haas = 'set output relay + M-FIN', would hang). Hurco WinMax ISNC: bare G84, always rigid-tap mode, NO M29. Okuma OSP: bare G84, controller auto-syncs spindle/feed, NO M29. RokuRoku Fanuc-31i: bare G84 + advisory warning (Fanuc 31i rigid tap technically needs M29 S<rpm> activation if not in persistent rigid-tap mode; engine emits bare G84 and warns -- does NOT fabricate M29 whose semantics differ per control setup, per R12). All 4 verified: emit probe 2026-06-28 (slot:echo) -- actual NC lines confirmed, not assumed.

latheJobsSchemaNote: Turning ops match the master_post_okuma_b250 zod schema (camActionSchemas.ts L159-198): operation_type (od_rough/od_finish/face/thread/groove/part_off/...), tool_number, tool_orientation (1-9), insert_radius_mm, material_iso, feed_mm_rev (mm/REV — turning), depth_of_cut_mm, start_x/start_z/end_x/end_z (X=diameter). G96 CSS via css_m_min + css_max_rpm (G50 clamp). Served to lathe + millturn posts (okuma-b250/lb3000/multus/winmax-lathe). CUT VALUES ARE SCHEMA-VALID TEST PLACEHOLDERS — production feeds/speeds come from SFC; lathe cut-physics + safety (G96→G50 cap, parting L/D, chuck) route to WHISKEY for review, not used as authoritative here.

liveToolJobsNote: C-axis driven-tool jobs (operation_type c_mill) that exercise OkumaB250's generateCAxisMilling path: M76 (C-axis home) + M23/M203 (live tool CW) + G12.1/G13.1 (polar interpolation on/off) + M24 (live tool off). Run ONLY against the C-axis-milling-capable JM lathes (GENOS-L300-M / GENOS-L200E-M / MULTUS-B250II, all -M / mill-turn); pure-turning lathes (LNC8/Crown/L400II-E) do NOT get C-axis jobs. use_css:false (live tool is G97 fixed RPM, not G96 CSS). The engine emits a REPRESENTATIVE polar pattern (engine line 905) -- full CAM-coordinate-driven C-axis toolpaths are a deeper enhancement; this verifies the live-tool emission is wired + dialect-clean + FNaN-safe for the machines that have the capability.

liveToolJobs.label: Live-tool C-axis slot (driven tool, M203 + G12.1 polar)

scoring.note: A post is 'perfect' when every corpus job scores structural 100% AND 0 dialect-lint ERRORs across all jobs. WARNs are advisory (feed-no-feedmode etc) — tracked, not failing, unless lintWarnPenalty raised.
